modern: Everything which is in any way beautiful is beautiful in itself, and complete in itself, not having praise as part of itself. A thing is made neither worse nor better by being praised. I say this also of the things which ordinary people call beautiful, for example, material things and works of art. That which is truly beautiful needs nothing; no more than law, no more than truth, no more than kindness or modesty. Which of these things is beautiful because it is praised, or spoiled by being blamed? Is something like an emerald made worse than it was if it is not praised? Or gold, ivory, purple, a lyre, a little knife, a flower, a shrub?
original: Everything which is in any way beautiful is beautiful in itself, and terminates in itself, not having praise as part of itself. That which is really beautiful has no need of anything; not more than law, not more than truth, not more than benevolence or modesty.
